chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Every person you include among your dependents, whether free or slave, upon you is to pay the Fitra on their behalf.
He (peace be upon him) said: And giving the Fitra before the Prayer is superior, and after the Prayer is (counted as) charity.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying Fitra for dependents and the difference between paying before and after the Eid prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the scope of Zakat al-Fitr by extending the obligation to all dependents, free or enslaved, under one's care, reflecting the comprehensive social welfare ethos of Shia jurisprudence. It establishes a critical legal distinction where pre-prayer payment fulfills the obligatory duty (ada), whereas post-prayer payment serves as voluntary charity (sadaqah), a nuance emphasized by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid to ensure the poor receive their share before the festive prayers commence.
